gen-dafont-origami-gf-cossette-texte: Origami looks brushed by a sign-painter in one constant stroke, its lowercase heavy as poured lead type. Cossette Texte follows in a sans with wide-eyed e shapes and a tall x-height, so a long passage goes down smoothly.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-duru-sans: Origami has the look of a round-tipped pen drawn in one width. Duru Sans, a modern sans-serif, wins on its wide small letters, bodies that dominate the line while ascenders barely show.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-fresca: Origami brings a single-stroke brush look and lowercase as dense as lead type. Fresca stays simple underneath, with connected counters and short ascenders over big bowls, so shrinking the heading would lose what makes it special.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-funnel-sans: Tight gaps between ascender tops and the x-height line give this body a compact, tidy look. Funnel Sans keeps its strokes constant from stem to curve, so a long passage feels steady beneath Origami's brushed heading.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-gafata: Origami draws every stroke with zero thick-and-thin contrast, like a brush held at one width, and its lowercase lands heavy. Gafata does the quieter job, a tall band of letters with short stalks.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-geist: Contemporary is the first word for Origami, a single-stroke brush hand with lowercase as dense as lead type. Geist sits next to it as a plain sans, level and quiet, its words forming solid blocks against that brushed heading.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-georama: Approachable describes Origami's flat, fineliner-like line, though its lowercase mass is dense and brushy. And Georama, a plain sans, keeps its capitals barely rising and its c pulled wide open.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-gidole: Think neon tube meets brush, with Origami drawing a single stroke and a lowercase heavy as lead type. But Gidole, a plain sans, keeps its terminals apart like open scissor blades and its midline set high.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-golos-text: Golos Text fills the line with a big x-height. Its strokes keep one width and its s parts widely, which sits comfortably against Origami's brushed single-stroke heading and dense lowercase.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-hedvig-letters-san: Approachable and a bit brushy, Origami writes in one constant stroke. Hedvig Letters Sans adds small letters nearly as tall as capitals and a clear gap where the c ends, giving the page a friendly, level footing.
